primary_locator: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41431-019-0494-2.pdf | ESHG 2019 p 1786 Clinical Genomics apps and GFM1 pediatric case series
assessment: The Clinical Genomics education poster refers to Apple and Android app stores. The GFM1 pediatric series separately finds dystonia among manifestations of pathogenic mitochondrial variants. Neither context evaluates food intake.

This German medical-abbreviation reference lists apple juice only as an expansion of AJO and cervical dystonia as a separate expansion of CD. The dictionary entries supply no exposure or outcome comparison.

primary_locator: https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1186/s12576-021-00809-x.pdf | physiology joint meeting PP-386 and symposium IS2
assessment: PP-386 analyzes phlorizin and endophytic fungi in the peel of Fuji apples grown under different farming conditions. The IS2 basal-ganglia symposium separately refers to dystonia and Parkinson disease when introducing circuit physiology. No baked-apple intervention is linked to dystonia.

B-0350 uses an Apple iPad and projector for children undergoing CT. A-563 discusses dystonia as a consequence of disrupted basal-ganglia circuits in a radiologic anatomy lecture. The Apple device serves as equipment.

primary_locator: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41386-019-0546-x.pdf | ACNP posters T82 pp 273–274 and T108 p 289
assessment: T82 uses a grape in a baited-bin rhesus-monkey fear assay to compare responses to a rubber snake. T108 separately measures daytime sleepiness and cognition in adolescents with ADHD. The grape serves as bait, without a frozen-grape sleepiness contrast.
